en: One Scroll on the Superior Characteristics of the Five-Syllable Mantra of Mañjuśrī, as Spoken in the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra: Transcending the Three Worlds*.
Compiled by the Grand Master of the Household, Peer of the State, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Sui.

The Imperial Preceptor, who held a fief of three thousand households, was conferred the rank of Grand Master (Sikong) with the purple robe, and posthumously granted the title of Great Mirror (Dajian) and the honorific name of Great Extensive Wisdom (Dayangzhi). Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple, by imperial decree. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi and all the other Bodhisattvas...
All of them, before Vairocana Buddha,
each spoke their own heart-mantra and mudrā.
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī—
Rising from his seat, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings of the future,
I now desire to swiftly attain the accomplishment of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā."
If a person recites it even once,
it is as if they have recited the eighty-four thousand twelve-fold Vedas;
if they recite it twice, [the merit is doubled].
Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra follow them,
surrounded by the fourfold assembly who bestow their empowerment;
the compassionate, fearless, and Dharma-protecting benevolent deities stand before such a person.
Ānanda addressed Mañjuśrī, saying:
"When this mantra was spoken,
ten trillion buddhas appeared."
In this manner, from each and every pore of these Buddhas, there emerge ten trillion bodhisattvas;
from each and every pore of each bodhisattva, there emerge ten trillion nāga kings;
and from each and every pore of each nāga king, there emerge ten trillion nāga maidens.
From every single pore of each dragon girl, there further emerged ten trillion blue elephants;
from every single pore of each blue elephant, there emerged ten trillion white elephants;
and from every single pore of each white elephant, there emerged ten trillion fragrant elephants.
From each pore of every fragrant elephant, there further emerged ten trillion mountain-elephants;
from each pore of every mountain-elephant,
there further manifested ten trillion jewel-enclosures.
Within each jeweled courtyard, there further appeared one hundred trillion ponds of water endowed with the eight virtues.
These ponds were composed of the four precious substances.
From each jeweled pond, one hundred trillion rays of Jāmbūnada gold light issued forth.
Furthermore, within each and every ray of light, there appeared one hundred trillion circular halos.
From each circular halo, one hundred trillion celestial maidens were manifested,
solemnly holding various kinds of offerings.
In this manner, the fourfold assemblies, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
gathered together in a great assembly at one time and spoke this mantra with a single voice.
I have now briefly described only a small portion of the samādhi of manifesting samādhis;
know that its merits are immeasurable.
Then he spoke the five-syllable mantra, saying:
"A-ra-pa-ca-na. O son of good family or daughter of good family, whoever is able to uphold this mantra..."
Upon reciting it even once, one immediately enters into the equality of all dharmas of the Tathāgata;
all letters and syllables are likewise equal,
and one swiftly attains the accomplishment of Mahāprajñā.
When bestowing this heart-mantra upon the disciples,
have them form the secret mudrā by binding the two hands in the vajra-bind.
Simultaneously form the mudrā of patience and vow by bending the upper joints into the shape of a sword;
place this mudrā upon the flower and scatter it as an offering upon the altar.
Then, one should address [the deity] as follows:
This Dharma-gate of the mind is the most supreme secret of all Tathāgatas.
Be careful not to speak of it lightly to foolish people;
it would destroy your samādhi and precepts.
Contemplate this well:
"A" signifies non-arising;
"Ra" signifies purity, freedom from defilement, and the state of being devoid of dust and impurity.
The "lame" refers to the meaning of the equality of all phenomena in the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*).
The "left" refers to the meaning that all phenomena are devoid of conditioned formations (*saṃskāra*).
The "ancient" refers to the fact that all phenomena are without intrinsic nature or characteristics (*lakṣaṇa*).
It is taught that all words and letters are unattainable in meaning,
because the letter *na* lacks intrinsic nature and characteristics,
and the letter *tsa* lacks all conditioned formations (*saṃskāra*).
Because the letter *la* is devoid of all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*),
the letter *pa* is devoid of the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*).
Because the letter *pa* is devoid of the ultimate truth...
The syllable *ra* is free from dust and defilement;
because the syllable *ra* is free from dust and defilement,
the syllable *a* signifies the meaning of the fundamental non-arising of phenomena.
"Good son, you should contemplate that this mind is fundamentally pure and free from all attachments.
It is devoid of the characteristics of conceptual discrimination regarding 'self' and 'what belongs to self.
Entering this gate is called samādhi."
This is true cultivation.
One should know that such a person is certified by the Tathāgata;
their sublime merit is inconceivable.
If one recites it once, all the practitioner’s hardships and difficulties will be eliminated.
If one recites it twice, the heavy sins of birth and death accumulated over billions of kalpas will be extinguished.
If one recites it three times, samādhi will manifest before them.
If one recites it four times, one will not forget the dhāraṇī;
if one recites it five times, one will swiftly attain unsurpassed bodhi.
If one can dwell alone in a quiet and secluded place with a single-minded focus, [the same result shall follow].
Having constructed a five-syllable wheel maṇḍala according to the Brahma-script and recited the mantra for one full month in accordance with the ritual,
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva will immediately manifest his body.
Or they may expound the essential teachings of the Dharma in mid-air.
At that time, the practitioner attains the knowledge of past lives,
unimpeded eloquence, and mastery of the supernormal powers.
With supreme vows accomplished and merit and wisdom fully perfected,
one will swiftly ascend to and realize the Tathāgata’s Dharmakāya;
it is sufficient merely to believe and accept this with the mind.
Within sixteen lifetimes, one will certainly attain perfect enlightenment.
If one lacks the capacity to establish a mandala,
make offerings of incense and flowers, or paint an image of the Honored One, [one may instead practice as follows].
Anoint the śarīra-stūpa with fragrant clay,
write the five-syllable mantra in Sanskrit characters,
and circumambulate it while reciting it five hundred thousand times.
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva will appear before that person and preach the Dharma for them;
they shall attain the eloquence of recollecting past lives,
as well as [the presence of] all Tathāgatas and bodhisattvas.
May the Vajradhara and the assembly of holy ones as numerous as the sands of the Ganges constantly bestow their protective mindfulness,
swiftly fulfilling all aspirations and enabling the rapid realization of Bodhi.
The details are as extensively explained in the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra*.
[This concludes] one fascicle on the supreme characteristics of Mañjuśrī’s Five-Syllable Mantra, as taught in the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra: Surpassing the Three Realms*.
